what_its_for: Omadacycline is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (a lung infection you can catch outside of a hospital) and skin and skin structure infections (such as infected wounds, abscesses, or cellulitis). It works by stopping the growth of bacteria that are causing your infection.
how_to_take: Omadacycline comes as a tablet that you swallow by mouth, or as an intravenous (IV) infusion given through a vein in your arm by a healthcare provider. For the tablet form: Take it on an EMPTY stomach — at least 4 hours after your last meal and at least 4 hours before your next meal or any dairy products, antacids, or vitamins. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, break, or chew the tablet. Take it at the same time each day. Take the full course of antibiotics even if you start feeling better early — stopping too soon can allow the infection to come back.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your infection type. A common adult dose for pneumonia tablets is 300 mg once daily. For skin infections, the starting dose is often higher and then reduced after a few days. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled dose time. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store omadacycline tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original packaging and away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it safely.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating food, drinking milk or dairy products, taking antacids (like Tums or Maalox), calcium supplements, iron supplements, multivitamins, or magnesium-containing products for at least 4 hours before and 4 hours after taking your omadacycline tablet — these can prevent the medication from being properly absorbed into your body. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight or tanning beds, as omadacycline can make your skin more sensitive to sunburn. Use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid taking this medication if you are pregnant unless your doctor says it is absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby, especially after the fourth month of pregnancy. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience any of the following: severe allergic reaction (hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing); severe skin reaction or rash; severe diarrhea or diarrhea that is watery or bloody (this could be a sign of a serious gut infection called C. difficile); yellowing of your skin or eyes; dark urine or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); dizziness, severe headache, or vision changes; signs of increased pressure in the skull (severe headache, blurred vision, ringing in ears); unusual bruising or bleeding; or any worsening of your symptoms or signs that your infection is not improving after a few days.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within the first 2 to 3 days of starting omadacycline. However, it is very important to finish the entire course of antibiotics as prescribed (usually 5 to 14 days depending on your infection), even if you feel completely better before you finish. Stopping early can cause your infection to return and may make it harder to treat.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This antibiotic can harm an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if omadacycline passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Omadacycline is not recommended for children under 18 years of age because antibiotics in this class can affect bone and tooth development in growing children. Older adults (65+): No special dose adjustment is typically needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your doctor may need to adjust your treatment plan.
